There Is No Biological Reason to Eat Three Meals a Day -- So Why Do We Do It?

Vietnamese have a longer "day" than the West, in general. The middle of the day is useless so it's often used as a "siesta," like in Spain. They often get up around 5:30, have breakfast (like pho or hu tieu) around 6, then go to work. Around 9 AM there will be a light meal, often fruit and a vegetable soup. Around noon there is another light meal, usually more soup but with a starch (noodles or rice) and often with a meat component. Around "tea time," there's fruit again. Then, at night, usually pretty late (7:30 or 8:00), there's a large meal. Works out pretty well.

I suppose the downside to this approach is when the masses start to choose to consume calorie dense Western foods at a similar frequency instead. I haven't been to Vietnam but the attitude of treating Western food as a highly desirable diet of a sign you'd "made it" was pretty rife in Cambodia and Laos.
